title: SplatBot Starter Pack
description: Starter missions for sequencing, turns, loops, sensors, debugging, coordinates, and early path planning.

missions.title: First Drive
missions.prompt: Move SplatBot from the start square to the gold goal. Count spaces before you run.
missions.teacherNote: Ask students to predict the number of spaces first, then run and compare the result.

missions.title: Turn the Corner
missions.prompt: Drive east, turn north, and reach the goal without leaving the field.
missions.teacherNote: Have students stand and turn their bodies before coding the turn block.

missions.title: Loop Lane
missions.prompt: Use a repeat block to make a short program that drives six spaces.
missions.teacherNote: Compare six move blocks with one repeat block to show why loops reduce repeated work.

missions.title: Box Route
missions.prompt: Drive around the block by combining movement, turns, and careful counting.
missions.teacherNote: Have students draw the route as short segments before they build blocks.

missions.title: Wall Sensor
missions.prompt: Use the wall-ahead sensor to make a decision before SplatBot bumps into the barrier.
missions.teacherNote: Pause near the wall and ask what information the robot has before the if block runs.

missions.title: Sensor Zigzag
missions.prompt: Use logic to steer around barriers. Watch the sensor readout after each step.
missions.teacherNote: Encourage students to run short attempts and revise one decision at a time.

missions.title: Coordinate Hop
missions.prompt: Use the position readout to navigate to column 7, row 7.
missions.teacherNote: Connect the readout to math grid vocabulary: x changes left-right, y changes up-down.

missions.title: Short Hop
missions.prompt: Move just two spaces. Stop before SplatBot passes the goal.
missions.teacherNote: Use this mission to show that more movement is not always better; the robot needs exact commands.

missions.title: Left Turn Lab
missions.prompt: Reach the goal using only left turns and move blocks.
missions.teacherNote: Students often count spaces correctly but forget the robot's facing direction. Keep the direction readout visible.

missions.title: Two-Side Turn
missions.prompt: Use a repeat-style pattern to move across two sides of a square corner.
missions.teacherNote: This is a good bridge from geometry to code: equal sides and turns can form larger shapes.

missions.title: Narrow Gate
missions.prompt: Drive through the open gate without touching the wall blocks.
missions.teacherNote: Ask students to run, observe the first problem, and change only one part before running again.

missions.title: U-Turn
missions.prompt: Turn around a dead end and guide SplatBot back toward the goal.
missions.teacherNote: A U-turn can be modeled as two same-direction turns. Let students discover that relationship.

missions.title: Sensor Checkpoint
missions.prompt: Use a sensor decision before each checkpoint turn.
missions.teacherNote: Introduce the idea that the same rule can be reused at more than one place in a program.

missions.title: Efficient Route
missions.prompt: Reach the goal with the fewest commands you can.
missions.teacherNote: Let pairs solve first, then compare command counts and discuss readability versus shortest code.

missions.title: Open Path
missions.prompt: Design a compact route that could later become a path-planning algorithm.
missions.teacherNote: Challenge older students to count commands and compare shorter versus clearer solutions.

missions.title: Sound Signal
missions.prompt: Reach the goal, turn on the signal light, and play a success sound.
missions.teacherNote: Connect sound and light feedback to everyday devices such as timers, crosswalks, and classroom alerts.
